title: weighted-grammar-sampler-and-token-boundary-reconciliation
author: Priya Nandakumar
description:
Motivation: We have recurring production failures when combining weighted CFG samplers with regex constraints on user-supplied patterns. Root cause analysis showed two related issues: (1) the weighted sampler could emit terminals that only partially align with tokenizer boundaries (BPE/bytefallthrough) which then caused regex backends to see partial tokens and fail constraint checks mid-stream; (2) the fallback logic into the simpler regex-only backend had a bias that triggered too late, causing streaming instability for long sequences. This PR introduces a reconciliation layer between grammar sampling and tokenizer-aware boundary checks plus a probabilistic early-fallback heuristic to keep streams healthy.

Summary of changes: single-string description of what changed and why. Implemented a "sampler-token-reconciliation" stage that performs lookahead sampling up to the model's maximum tokenization window and rejects candidate derivations that would split tokens in a way that violates active regex constraints. Added a weighted-sampler adjustment that considers terminal tokenization length distributions (collected from model tokenizer profiles) so higher-probability grammar choices that lead to awkward token splits are penalized. Added an early-fallback controller that switches to the regex-only constrained backend when the sampler's rejection rate exceeds a threshold or when KV cache hit patterns indicate pathological streaming behavior. Updated test harness with targeted fuzz cases that reproduce previously-observed production failures. Instrumented metrics: constraint_reject_rate, early_fallback_count, boundary_mismatch_samples, and sampler_candidate_latency.

Why this is different from prior work: existing fixes addressed token-boundary heuristics in the regex backend or isolated tokenizer shims. This PR couples grammar-level sampling decisions with tokenizer statistics and introduces a lightweight early-fallback policy to prevent streaming stalls without sacrificing structured-output correctness.

Migration notes: behavior change is backward-compatible by default; customers that pinned to older CFG-weighting semantics may see slightly different sampling probabilities in edge cases (where token-split penalties apply). The default thresholds are conservative and documented in the release notes.

Related: ENG-4512 (regression triage), ENG-4638 (streaming incident follow-up).

review_conversation:
Alexei Volkov (reviewer): Can you explain why we need offline token-length histograms instead of sampling live from the tokenizer?

Priya Nandakumar (author): Offline histograms let us cheaply estimate tokenization costs without invoking tokenizer hot paths in the hot loop; we refresh profiles regularly in background jobs. Live tokenization in the sampler caused measurable latency regressions in internal experiments.

Jordan Li (reviewer): The early-fallback threshold looks magic-numbery; can we make it a per-model config and add an admin toggle in the console?

Priya Nandakumar (author): Agreed. Made it a per-model config with sane defaults and added a console flag for operators. See config entry fl.sampler_early_fallback.threshold and the docs change.

Marta Ruiz (reviewer): Are there metrics to detect if the reconciliation is over-constraining generation (false negatives)?

Priya Nandakumar (author): Added constraint_reject_rate and boundary_mismatch_samples. Also added an automated alert that fires if constraint_reject_rate > 0.02 sustained for 10m.

Alexei Volkov: Approved after minor nits. Jordan Li: Approved. Marta Ruiz: Approved with one remark on test naming (fixed).
release_notes: Fix: grammar sampler now accounts for tokenizer boundary costs to prevent partial-token constraint failures; add early-fallback to regex backend to improve streaming stability. Metrics added: constraint_reject_rate, early_fallback_count. Impact: non-breaking default, minor sampling probability changes in rare edge cases.
